novelty_flags.label: Theorem hazard-lift-identification and related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: The causal-latent-Markov comparison omits closer published work: Pennoni, Paas, and Bartolucci (2023) develops causal HMM effects for repeatedly assigned time-varying treatments, and Clouth et al. (2025) uses a latent Markov model within a causal g-formula; distinguish their model-based latent-state recovery from the proposed observable alias-fiber invariant.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition exact-fiber-gap and Proposition collision-gray-zone
soundness_flags.one_line: Both claims assert a one-step cohort-mean/ATT separation without binding the cohort index g, and the exact-fiber definition also omits the horizon; specify the supported g and T for which every displayed equality and 2/185 gap is claimed.

soundness_flags.label: Open-ended Question legal-lift-frontier
soundness_flags.one_line: The displayed singleton set mixes path laws pi^0_{g,r} over different r, hence different sample spaces; require instead that for every fixed (g,r), the set over legal J is a singleton, or define a common stacked product object.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition standard-reductions
soundness_flags.one_line: “Geometric-hazard plug-in” and “usual full-recovery branch” are undefined labels; replace them with the explicit K=1 and distinct-emission formulas so the claimed reductions are checkable.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem hazard-lift-identification
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The result is conditional on known finite K, finite alphabet, T >= 2K-1, homogeneous untreated dynamics, stopped-rank/invertibility, sequential hazard randomization, and the novel within-emission-profile hazard restriction.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Identifies finite cohort counterfactual path laws only within the declared hazard-lift panel class; it does not claim latent-label or unrestricted-HMM recovery.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem fixed-chart-inference
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Inference is conditional on one fixed declared chart and frame with observable separation, support, moment, and variance margins and excludes the stated collision path.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Uniform root-N linearization and simultaneous coverage hold only on compact separated subsets of P_kappa, not across algebra/rank collisions.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies parametric-output HMMs with exactly two aliased states and gives a characterization of minimality and identifiability for that class.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Computer and System Sciences 78(5), 2012
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article gives a spectral HMM learning result under smallest-singular-value separation conditions.
The article proposes a discrete-time event-history extension of a mixed latent-Markov model for informative dropout.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Publisher bibliographic record and abstract; pp. 200–230
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper addresses identification, estimation, and simultaneous bootstrap inference for staggered DiD under conditional parallel-trends assumptions.
The paper uses treatment-timing variation and an interactive-fixed-effects focus to identify a large class of staggered-adoption causal parameters without parallel trends.
The paper proposes ATT identification from repeated outcomes under a framework allowing multidimensional and non-additively separable unobservables.
The paper develops reverse-time nested matching for staggered group- and time-specific effects and applies it to Netflix–IPTV data.

source_verification_receipts.version: Sociological Methods & Research version of record, 2025
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article gives causal latent-Markov/g-formula ATE and natural-course ATT procedures, explicitly modeling exposure and latent-state dynamics under exchangeability, positivity, consistency, Markovianity, and conditional independence.

The article develops a causal HMM for repeatedly assigned time-varying marketing treatments, defines latent potential outcomes, and uses propensity-weighted model fitting under exogeneity/positivity assumptions.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Pennoni–Paas–Bartolucci (2023), Tullio–Bartolucci (2022), and Clouth et al. (2025) to related work and state a precise non-subsumption comparison: their causal HMMs posit latent-state model recovery under ignorability, whereas this target is an observed stopped-law functional invariant across legal non-permutation alias fibers.
Repair every cohort-indexed negative construction by fixing g and T in its definition and reporting the exact stopped-word equality, positivity inequalities, and ATT difference for that same g.

Restate the legal-lift OEQ as componentwise singleton identification over J, then specify the finite semialgebraic input encoding, output certificate, and a termination/complexity target for fixed K,T,|Y|.

Add a theorem-level comparison showing a regime where the observable hazard-lift functional identifies ATT although the listed causal-HMM approaches cannot be applied because latent recovery or observed-confounder ignorability fails.

recommended_next_step: Revise the malformed cohort/fiber statements and broaden the causal-HMM survey with explicit non-subsumption comparisons, then continue this field-tier angle to Stage 0.
